title: Degree-zero normalization of abelian Čech comparisons
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\iota$ a type, $U_i$ a family of opens with $\sup_i U_i=X$, and $F$ an abelian sheaf [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology]. Let $c:\check H^0(U,F)\to H^0(X,F)$ be an additive map satisfying IsAbelianCechComparison in degree zero [def-pc-abelian-cech-comparison-construction]. Then $c$ equals the inverse of the canonical restriction isomorphism $F(X)\to\check H^0(U,F)$ [lem-pc-topological-cech-zero-gluing-iso], followed by the inverse of the canonical Ext-zero-to-sections isomorphism. No comparison in another degree and no quasi-isomorphism hypothesis on $\alpha$ is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 20.11.2, construction of H(beta) H(alpha) inverse and independence of the resolution

proof.text: For each Čech zero class x, let b be Ext.addEquiv₀(c(x)), a morphism from the constant integer sheaf to F, and let s be its adjoint evaluated at 1. Thus Ext.mk₀(b)=c(x), and functorHZeroIso sends c(x) to s. Fix the existing injectiveResolution F. The map a=b followed by I.ι.f 0 is a cocycle. Prove extMk(a)=Ext.mk₀(b) directly using InjectiveResolution.extMk_hom: the fromSingleMk cocycle corresponds under equivHomShift to the single-complex map of b followed by I.ι prime; after localization, I.ι prime cancels its inverse. Lift the section augmentation of s to a cycle z using liftCycles. Adjunction.homEquiv_naturality_right and liftCycles_i identify iCycles(z) with the adjoint of a evaluated at 1. Apply the assumed quotient equation hc to x,a,z.

Prove the augmentation square on zero cohomology: restriction followed by H(beta) equals the section augmentation into cycles followed by homologyπ and H(alpha). Rewrite homologyπ_naturality, cancel the degree-zero total homology projection and cycle inclusion, and apply liftCycles_i. The remaining cochain equality is precisely restriction naturality of I.ι.f 0. Also prove H(beta) is monic: its degree-zero cochain component is the product of the sectionwise monomorphisms induced by I.ι.f 0, followed by a split-monic coproduct inclusion. Since no differential enters degree zero, Mathlib mono_homologyMap_of_mono_of_not_rel yields the claim. Comparing the augmentation square at s with the quotient equation and cancelling H(beta) gives x=toCechCohomologyZero(s).

The covering condition makes toCechCohomologyZero the hom of cechCohomologyZeroIso. Apply its inverse to x=toCechCohomologyZero(s), obtaining s=cechCohomologyZeroIso.inv(x). This proves c followed by functorHZeroIso.hom equals cechCohomologyZeroIso.inv on every element. Cancel functorHZeroIso.hom to obtain the required equality of additive morphisms. The argument uses no nonempty or finite cover hypothesis and no quasi-isomorphism statement about alpha.

from.place: Proof step 3: degree-zero normalization from the quotient equation

lean.statement:
theorem abelianCechComparison_zero_normalization
    {X : Scheme.{u}} {ι : Type u} (U : ι → X.Opens) (hcover : iSup U = ⊤)
    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{u})
    (c : (TopCat.Sheaf.cechCohomologyFunctor U 0).obj F ⟶
      (Sheaf.functorH (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) 0).obj F)
    (hc : IsAbelianCechComparison U F 0 c) :
    c = (TopCat.Sheaf.cechCohomologyZeroIso U hcover).inv.app F ≫
      (Sheaf.functorHZeroIso (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) isTerminalTop).inv.app F
